subject: biology
label: 2022 Sem 1
instructions: All questions are compulsory. The marks intended for questions are given in brackets [ ]. Select the correct option for each question.

questions.question: Name the following by choosing the correct option: The process of conversion of ADP to ATP during photosynthesis:
questions.solution: Option (b) Photophosphorylation. Photophosphorylation is the conversion of ADP to ATP using light energy during the light phase of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Name the following by choosing the correct option: Permanently open structures seen on the barks of old woody stems:
questions.solution: Option (c) Lenticels. Lenticels are permanently open pores on the bark of old woody stems; they allow gaseous exchange.

questions.question: Name the following by choosing the correct option: The pressure developed in the roots due to continuous inward movement of water by cell to cell osmosis:
questions.solution: Option (a) Root pressure. Root pressure is the pressure developed in roots due to continued inward movement of water by cell to cell osmosis.

questions.question: Name the following by choosing the correct option: The type of gene, which in the presence of a contrasting allele is not expressed:
questions.solution: Option (d) Recessive. A recessive gene is not expressed in the presence of its contrasting (dominant) allele. Printed key says (b) Heterozygous, but its own explanation says Recessive; correct answer is (d).

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: Name the following by choosing the correct option: After Mitosis, a female human cell will have:
questions.solution: Option (a) 44 + XX chromosomes. Mitosis is equational division, so daughter cells of a human female cell have 44 + XX chromosomes.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: Complete the following statement by choosing the appropriate option for the blank: At the end of ______, Cytokinesis is completed.
questions.solution: Option (d) Telophase. Cytokinesis begins in anaphase and is completed at the end of telophase.

questions.question: Complete the following statement by choosing the appropriate option for the blank: The genotype of a person who cannot roll his tongue is ____.
questions.solution: Option (c) rr. Tongue rolling is dominant (R); a non-roller is homozygous recessive, rr.

questions.question: Complete the following statement by choosing the appropriate option for the blank: When a cell is placed in a ______ solution, it becomes plasmolysed.
questions.solution: Option (b) Hypertonic. In a hypertonic solution the plant cell loses water and shrinks, i.e. is plasmolysed.

questions.question: Complete the following statement by choosing the appropriate option for the blank: The nitrogenous base Adenine always pairs with _______.
questions.solution: Option (a) Thymine. Adenine always pairs with thymine (guanine with cytosine).

questions.question: Complete the following statement by choosing the appropriate option for the blank: The basic units of heredity are _______.
questions.solution: Option (c) Genes. A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer from the four options given below: NADP is expanded as:
questions.solution: Option (b) Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate. NADP = Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer from the four options given below: Transpiration is useful to the plant because it:

options.a: Creates a suction force for absorption of water from the soil.

questions.solution: Option (a) Creates a suction force for absorption of water from the soil. Transpiration creates a suction pull that draws water up from the roots through xylem.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer from the four options given below: A homozygous pea plant having purple flowers is crossed with a homozygous pea plant bearing white flowers. The phenotypic ratio of the offspring obtained in F2 generation is:
questions.solution: Option (d) 3 : 1. F2 phenotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross is 3 purple : 1 white, i.e. 3:1.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer from the four options given below: A shoot from a balsam plant is kept in a beaker containing eosin solution (pink). The pink colour will be distinctly seen in the:
questions.solution: Option (a) Xylem. Eosin enters the xylem vessels, which show pink/red, proving water uptake is through xylem.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: Choose the correct answer from the four options given below: Replication of DNA in the cell cycle occurs during the:
questions.solution: Option (c) S-phase. DNA replication occurs in the S-phase.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: Explain the following term by choosing the correct option: Karyokinesis:

options.a: It is the division of nucleus during cell division.
options.b: It is the division of cytoplasm during cell division.
options.c: It is the division of centrosome.
options.d: It is the division of nucleolus.

questions.solution: Option (a) It is the division of nucleus during cell division. Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus during cell division; it is followed by cytokinesis.

questions.question: Explain the following term by choosing the correct option: Law of Dominance:

options.a: Out of a pair of contrasting alleles present together, only the recessive allele is able to express itself while the dominant remains suppressed.
options.b: Out of a pair of contrasting alleles present together, only the dominant allele is able to express itself while the recessive remains suppressed.
options.c: Out of a pair of contrasting alleles present together, both the dominant and recessive cannot express themselves.
options.d: Out of a pair of contrasting alleles present together, both the dominant and recessive can express themselves.

questions.solution: Option (b) Out of a pair of contrasting alleles present together, only the dominant allele is able to express itself while the recessive remains suppressed. Law of dominance: of a pair of contrasting alleles only the dominant expresses itself; the recessive remains suppressed.

questions.question: Explain the following term by choosing the correct option: Mutation:

options.a: It is a sudden change in one or more genes in an organism's cells which is heritable.
options.b: It is a change in the number of centrosomes in an organism's cells which is heritable.
options.c: It is a change in the structure of cell membrane in an organism's cell which is heritable.
options.d: It is a change in the shape of cells which is heritable.

questions.solution: Option (a) It is a sudden change in one or more genes in an organism's cells which is heritable. Mutation is a sudden heritable change in one or more genes (DNA sequence).

questions.question: Explain the following term by choosing the correct option: Photosynthesis:

options.a: It is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide by non-green plants using light energy.
options.b: It is the synthesis of glucose by green plants from carbon dioxide using light energy.
options.c: It is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water by non-green plants using light energy.
options.d: It is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water by green plants using light energy.

questions.solution: Option (d) It is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water by green plants using light energy. Photosynthesis is the synthesis of glucose from carbon dioxide and water by green plants using light energy.

questions.question: Explain the following term by choosing the correct option: Transpiration:

options.a: It is the loss of water in the form of droplets from the aerial parts of the plant.
options.b: It is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the underground parts of the plant.
options.c: It is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant.
options.d: It is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from all parts of the plant.

questions.solution: Option (d) It is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from all parts of the plant. Transpiration is loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant, mainly via stomata.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
concepts: aster around centrioles in animal cells
questions.question: Mention the exact location of the following: Aster:

options.a: Around the centrioles in plant cells.
options.b: Around the centrioles in animal cells.
options.c: Around the chromatids in animal cells.
options.d: Around the chromatids in plant cells.

questions.solution: Option (b) Around the centrioles in animal cells. Aster is a star-shaped structure around the centrioles in animal cells.

questions.question: Mention the exact location of the following: Guard cells:
questions.solution: Option (d) Around the stoma. Guard cells surround the stoma.

questions.question: Mention the exact location of the following: Xylem tissue:

options.a: Conducts water and minerals in leaves.
options.b: Does not conduct water and minerals in stems.
options.c: Conducts food and nutrients to roots.
options.d: Conducts food and nutrients to all parts of the plant.

questions.solution: Option (a) Conducts water and minerals in leaves. Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals from roots to aerial parts such as leaves.

questions.question: Mention the exact location of the following: Centrioles:

options.d: Found in animal and plant cells.

questions.solution: Option (c) Found only in animal cells. Centrioles are found only in animal cells, in the cytoplasm near the nuclear envelope.

questions.question: Mention the exact location of the following: Genes:
questions.solution: Option (c) Present on chromosomes. Genes are present on chromosomes in the nucleus.

concepts: cell wall function in plant cells
questions.question: State the functions of the following: Cell wall:

options.a: Regulates entry of solutes in plant cells.
options.b: Regulates entry of solutes in animal cells.
options.c: Gives rigidity and shape to plant cells.
options.d: Gives rigidity and shape to animal cells.

questions.solution: Option (c) Gives rigidity and shape to plant cells. The plant cell wall gives rigidity and shape to plant cells.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: State the functions of the following: Centromere:

options.a: It is the point of attachment of two sister chromatids.
options.b: It is the point of attachment of two centrioles.
options.c: It is the point of attachment of two centrosomes.
options.d: It is the point of attachment between two daughter nuclei.

questions.solution: Option (a) It is the point of attachment of two sister chromatids. The centromere is the point of attachment of two sister chromatids.

questions.question: State the functions of the following: Cuticle on leaves:
questions.solution: Option (b) Reduces transpiration. The cuticle is a water-impervious layer that reduces transpiration.

questions.question: State the functions of the following: Hydathodes:
questions.solution: Option (d) Guttation. Hydathodes discharge water from the leaf interior to its surface: guttation.

concepts: grana light-dependent phase vs stroma dark phase
questions.question: State the functions of the following: Grana of chloroplast is not the:
questions.solution: Option (a) Site of Light Independent Phase. Grana are the site of the light-dependent phase (photon absorption, photolysis), not the light-independent phase.

questions.question: The diagram given below represents an experiment to demonstrate a particular aspect of photosynthesis. The letter 'A' indicates a certain condition inside the flask. (Diagram: a potted plant with a leaf (leaf 1) enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution, and another leaf (leaf 2) exposed to air outside the flask.) Answer the question: What is the aim of the experiment?

options.a: To show that oxygen is released during Photosynthesis.
options.b: To show that Photosynthesis occurs in the presence of KOH.
options.c: To show that chlorophyll is necessary for Photosynthesis.
options.d: To show that carbon dioxide is necessary for Photosynthesis.

questions.solution: Option (d) To show that carbon dioxide is necessary for Photosynthesis. KOH absorbs CO2; absence of CO2 means no starch, showing CO2 is necessary for photosynthesis.
questions.figure_desc: Potted plant with one leaf enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution (condition A) and another leaf exposed to air.

questions.question: The diagram given below represents an experiment to demonstrate a particular aspect of photosynthesis. The letter 'A' indicates a certain condition inside the flask. (Diagram: a potted plant with a leaf (leaf 1) enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution, and another leaf (leaf 2) exposed to air outside the flask.) Answer the question: What is the special condition inside the flask?

options.a: Air inside the flask is free of oxygen.
options.b: Air inside the flask is free of carbon dioxide.
options.c: Air inside the flask is free of nitrogen.
options.d: KOH purifies the air inside the flask.

questions.solution: Option (b) Air inside the flask is free of carbon dioxide. KOH absorbs all CO2, so air in the flask is free of carbon dioxide.
questions.figure_desc: Same set-up: leaf in a flask containing KOH solution, labelled condition A.

questions.question: The diagram given below represents an experiment to demonstrate a particular aspect of photosynthesis. The letter 'A' indicates a certain condition inside the flask. (Diagram: a potted plant with a leaf (leaf 1) enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution, and another leaf (leaf 2) exposed to air outside the flask.) Answer the question: An alternative chemical that can be used instead of KOH is:
questions.solution: Option (a) Sodium hydroxide. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) also absorbs CO2.

concepts: starch test result in control vs experimental leaf
questions.question: The diagram given below represents an experiment to demonstrate a particular aspect of photosynthesis. The letter 'A' indicates a certain condition inside the flask. (Diagram: a potted plant with a leaf (leaf 1) enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution, and another leaf (leaf 2) exposed to air outside the flask.) Answer the question: In what manner do the leaves 1 and 2 differ at the end of the starch test?

options.a: Leaf 1 turns brown, Leaf 2 turns blue black.
options.b: Leaf 1 turns blue black, Leaf 2 turns brown.
options.c: Leaf 1 turns purple, Leaf 2 remains green.
options.d: There is no change in the colour of the leaves.

questions.solution: Option (a) Leaf 1 turns brown, Leaf 2 turns blue black. Leaf 1 (in flask, no CO2) has no starch so iodine stays brown; leaf 2 turns blue-black.
questions.figure_desc: Same set-up: leaf 1 inside KOH flask, leaf 2 outside; both tested with iodine.

questions.question: The diagram given below represents an experiment to demonstrate a particular aspect of photosynthesis. The letter 'A' indicates a certain condition inside the flask. (Diagram: a potted plant with a leaf (leaf 1) enclosed in a flask containing KOH solution, and another leaf (leaf 2) exposed to air outside the flask.) Answer the question: What is the important step that should be taken before performing this experiment?

options.a: The plant should be placed in dark for 24 hours to destarch the entire plant.
options.b: The plant should be placed in dark for 24 hours to remove chlorophyll from the leaves.
options.c: The plant should be placed in dark for 24 hours to destarch the leaves.
options.d: The plant should be placed in dark for 24 hours for the roots to absorb water.

questions.solution: Option (c) The plant should be placed in dark for 24 hours to destarch the leaves. The plant is kept in dark for 24-48 hours to destarch the leaves.

concepts: cobalt chloride paper experiment aim, stomata distribution
questions.question: Given below is the diagram of an experimental setup to study the process of Transpiration. Cobalt chloride papers are fixed on the upper as well as lower surface of the leaf. Answer the question that follows: What is the aim of the experiment?

options.a: To prove that more transpiration occurs from the lower surface of a dicot leaf.
options.b: To prove that more transpiration occurs from the upper surface of a dicot leaf.
options.c: To prove that transpiration is equal on both sides of the leaf.
options.d: To prove that transpiration does not take place in a dicot leaf.

questions.solution: Option (a) To prove that more transpiration occurs from the lower surface of a dicot leaf. More transpiration occurs from the lower surface of a dicot leaf due to more stomata.

questions.topic: Colour of dry cobalt chloride paper
concepts: dry cobalt chloride paper colour blue
questions.question: Given below is the diagram of an experimental setup to study the process of Transpiration. Cobalt chloride papers are fixed on the upper as well as lower surface of the leaf. Answer the question that follows: What is the colour of dry cobalt chloride paper?
questions.solution: Option (b) Blue. Dry cobalt chloride paper is blue.

concepts: cobalt chloride blue to pink, more stomata on lower surface
questions.question: Given below is the diagram of an experimental setup to study the process of Transpiration. Cobalt chloride papers are fixed on the upper as well as lower surface of the leaf. Answer the question that follows: After about an hour, what change if any, would you expect to find in the cobalt chloride paper placed on the upper and lower surface of the leaf?

options.a: Upper surface - Pink, Lower Surface - Blue.
options.b: Upper surface - White, Lower surface - Blue.
options.c: Upper surface - less pink, Lower surface - more pink.
options.d: Upper surface - more pink, Lower surface - less pink.

questions.solution: Option (c) Upper surface - less pink, Lower surface - more pink. Lower surface paper turns more pink (more stomata); upper surface less pink.

questions.question: Given below is the diagram of an experimental setup to study the process of Transpiration. Cobalt chloride papers are fixed on the upper as well as lower surface of the leaf. Answer the question that follows: Two adaptations in plants to reduce Transpiration are:

options.b: Fewer stomata, Broad lamina of leaves.

questions.solution: Option (d) Narrow leaves, Fewer stomata. Narrow leaves and fewer stomata reduce transpiration.

concepts: factors affecting transpiration rate: humidity, temperature
questions.question: Given below is the diagram of an experimental setup to study the process of Transpiration. Cobalt chloride papers are fixed on the upper as well as lower surface of the leaf. Answer the question that follows: The rate of transpiration is less when there is:

options.a: High humidity in the air and low temperature.
options.b: Less humidity in the air and decrease in atmospheric pressure.
options.d: More wind and low intensity of sunlight.

questions.solution: Option (a) High humidity in the air and low temperature. Transpiration is less when humidity is high and temperature is low.
